questions.prompt: Determine whether \(\{(1,0),(0,1)\}\) is a basis of \(\mathbb R^2\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The vectors are independent and every \((x,y)=x(1,0)+y(0,1)\).
Final answer: The set is a basis of \(\mathbb R^2\).

questions.prompt: Calculate the coordinates of \((3,-2)\) in the basis \(B=\{(1,0),(1,1)\}\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Set \(a(1,0)+b(1,1)=(3,-2)\). Then \(b=-2\) and \(a+b=3\), so \(a=5\).
Final answer: \([(3,-2)]_B=(5,-2)\).

questions.prompt: Determine the dimension of \(P_3\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The monomials \(1,x,x^2,x^3\) form a basis, containing four vectors.
Final answer: \(\dim P_3=4\).

questions.prompt: Construct a basis for \(\{(x,y,z):x+y+z=0\}\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Let \(y=s,z=t\), giving \(x=-s-t\):
\[(x,y,z)=s(-1,1,0)+t(-1,0,1).\]
Final answer: A basis is \(\{(-1,1,0),(-1,0,1)\}\).

questions.prompt: Determine the dimension of the diagonal \(3\times3\) real matrices.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Every diagonal matrix is \(aE_{11}+bE_{22}+cE_{33}\), and these three matrices are independent.
Final answer: The dimension is \(3\).

questions.prompt: Construct a basis for the symmetric \(2\times2\) real matrices.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Every symmetric matrix is
\[\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}=a\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}+b\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}+c\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.\]
Final answer: The three displayed matrices form a basis.

questions.prompt: Calculate the coordinates of \(p(x)=2-x+3x^2\) in \(B=\{1+x,x,x^2\}\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Set \(a(1+x)+bx+cx^2=p\). Coefficients give \(a=2\), \(a+b=-1\), \(c=3\), hence \(b=-3\).
Final answer: \([p]_B=(2,-3,3)\).

questions.prompt: Determine whether \(\{(1,1),(1,-1)\}\) is a basis of \(\mathbb R^2\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The determinant of the column matrix is \(-1-1=-2\ne0\), so the vectors are independent and span \(\mathbb R^2\).
Final answer: The set is a basis.

questions.prompt: Find the dimension of \(S=\{p\in P_3:p(0)=0\}\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The condition removes the constant coefficient, so \(p=ax+bx^2+cx^3\). A basis is \(\{x,x^2,x^3\}\).
Final answer: \(\dim S=3\).

questions.prompt: Construct a basis for the column space of \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&0&1\\1&2&1\end{pmatrix}\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The second column is twice the first. The first and third columns are independent.
Final answer: A basis is \(\{(1,0,1)^{\mathsf T},(0,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\}\).

questions.prompt: Determine a basis and dimension for the null space of \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&-1\\0&1&1\end{pmatrix}\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The equations give \(y=-z\) and \(x-2z-z=0\), so \(x=3z\). Thus \(\mathbf x=z(3,-1,1)\).
Final answer: A basis is \(\{(3,-1,1)\}\), and the dimension is \(1\).

questions.prompt: Construct a basis of \(\mathbb R^3\) by extending \(\{(1,1,0),(0,1,1)\}\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Add \((1,0,0)\). The determinant
\[\begin{vmatrix}1&0&1\\1&1&0\\0&1&0\end{vmatrix}=1\ne0.\]
Final answer: One extension is \(\{(1,1,0),(0,1,1),(1,0,0)\}\).

questions.prompt: Construct a basis for the span of \(\{(1,0,1),(0,1,1),(1,1,2),(1,-1,0)\}\) by reducing the set.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The third vector is the sum of the first two and the fourth is their difference. The first two are independent.
Final answer: A basis is \(\{(1,0,1),(0,1,1)\}\).

questions.prompt: Determine the dimension of the solution space of \(x+y+z+w=0\) in \(\mathbb R^4\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
There is one independent homogeneous constraint on four variables. Explicitly,
\[(x,y,z,w)=y(-1,1,0,0)+z(-1,0,1,0)+w(-1,0,0,1).\]
Final answer: The dimension is \(3\).

questions.prompt: Determine all \(k\) for which \(B_k=\{(1,0,1),(0,1,1),(1,1,k)\}\) is a basis of \(\mathbb R^3\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The column determinant is
\[\begin{vmatrix}1&0&1\\0&1&1\\1&1&k\end{vmatrix}=k-2.\]
A basis requires nonzero determinant.
Final answer: \(B_k\) is a basis for \(k\ne2\).

questions.prompt: Calculate the change-of-coordinate matrix from \(B=\{(1,1),(1,-1)\}\) to the standard basis.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The columns are the basis vectors written in standard coordinates, so
\[P_{E\leftarrow B}=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.\]
Final answer: \(P_{E\leftarrow B}=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}\).

questions.prompt: Prove that every basis of a finite-dimensional vector space has the same number of vectors.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Let one basis have \(m\) vectors and another have \(n\). Since the first basis is independent and the second spans, the replacement theorem gives \(m\le n\). Reversing their roles gives \(n\le m\). Therefore \(m=n\).
Final answer: All bases have the same cardinality.

questions.prompt: Prove the rank-nullity formula for a linear map \(T:V\to W\) with finite-dimensional \(V\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Choose a basis \(\{\mathbf k_1,\ldots,\mathbf k_r\}\) for \(\ker T\) and extend it to a basis of \(V\) by \(\mathbf v_1,\ldots,\mathbf v_s\). The vectors \(T\mathbf v_1,\ldots,T\mathbf v_s\) span \(\operatorname{im}T\), and a relation among them would put a nontrivial combination of the \(\mathbf v_j\) in the kernel, contradicting the basis. Thus they form an image basis. Hence \(\dim V=r+s\).
Final answer: \(\dim V=\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{im}T\).

questions.prompt: Prove that an independent set of \(n\) vectors in an \(n\)-dimensional space is a basis.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
If the set did not span, choose \(\mathbf v\) outside its span. Adding \(\mathbf v\) would give \(n+1\) independent vectors, impossible in an \(n\)-dimensional space.
Final answer: Every independent \(n\)-vector set in an \(n\)-dimensional space is a basis.

questions.prompt: Prove the dimension formula \(\dim(U+W)=\dim U+\dim W-\dim(U\cap W)\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Choose a basis \(\{\mathbf z_1,\ldots,\mathbf z_r\}\) of \(U\cap W\). Extend it by \(\mathbf u_1,\ldots,\mathbf u_p\) to a basis of \(U\), and by \(\mathbf w_1,\ldots,\mathbf w_q\) to a basis of \(W\). The combined list \(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf u_j,\mathbf w_k\) is a basis of \(U+W\), so
\[\dim(U+W)=r+p+q=(r+p)+(r+q)-r.\]
Final answer: \(\dim(U+W)=\dim U+\dim W-\dim(U\cap W)\).
